description: A phase-modulation operator: one sine oscillator whose phase can be pushed by another signal, running sixteen polyphonic channels

params.text: Sets how many semitones of pitch one volt at V/OCT gives, 1 to 48; at 12 the oscillator tracks an octave per volt
Transposes the oscillator by a fixed amount before the scaling is applied, 0 to 128 semitones
Scales what the PM input does to the phase, from fully inverted through nothing to fully positive; the dial's travel is cubed and the result reaches 32 radians per volt
Adds a fixed offset to the oscillator's phase, from minus pi to plus pi radians

inputs.text: Shifts the oscillator's phase in proportion to its voltage, by the amount the modulation index sets
A rising crossing through 0V here restarts the oscillator's cycle from phase zero
Sets the pitch; the number of channels patched here is the number of channels the module runs

outputs.text: A sine wave taken from the oscillator's phase, swinging 10V either way

notes: the scaled pitch is clipped at zero, so once the offset and scale bring the total down to nothing the frequency stops falling however negative the voltage at V/OCT goes
the lowest frequency the oscillator reaches is 440Hz divided by 128, and every volt of scaled pitch doubles it from there

inputs.1:
high above 0V · stepped · polyphonic

a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.2:
1V per octave · continuous · polyphonic

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
